definition: In mental health care, patients’ rights are the legal or formal protections and information that people receiving care are entitled to be told about. In this context, the term refers especially to informing involuntary psychiatric patients of their rights when they are admitted.

reasons: The definition generalizes beyond the packet by defining patients’ rights broadly as “legal or formal protections” and as information all people receiving care are entitled to be told about; the packet only supports rights information being given to involuntary psychiatric patients upon admission in British Columbia.
The specific sense needed here is too narrow and context-specific in the packet to support the broader first-sentence definition as written.

The packet only describes clinicians’ responsibility to provide “rights information” to involuntary psychiatric patients upon admission and an Ombudsperson investigation about that responsibility; it does not explicitly support the broader wording that patients’ rights are “legal or formal protections” or that they apply generally to “people receiving care.”
The definition’s first sentence contains substantive claims (“legal or formal protections” and entitlement for people receiving care) that are not directly stated in the supplied packet.
